facts_zh:
AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
- Published
Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have been climbing following an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday.
Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.

articles.title_original: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
articles.title_zh: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
facts_zh:
Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
- Published
More than two dozen Democrats are eyeing runs for the White House in 2028, following their party's success in the US midterm elections this week, according to the man behind Barack Obama's successful re-election bid.

Jim Messina, who led Obama's 2012 campaign, said that since Democrats saw major victories in congressional races as well as state elections, he's spoken to "over two dozen campaigns" that are actively considering running in 2028 and have begun the financing process and hiring staff.
"I think you're going to start having Democrats announce exploratory committees next week or the next couple of weeks, probably after Thanksgiving", Messina told the BBC's Americast podcast.

all_titles.en: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide

articles.title_zh: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
facts_zh:
Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
- Published
A young girl and an 18-year-old man have died after a bus crashed in eastern France, local authorities have said.
The bus was travelling between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse when it crashed at around 07:00 local time on Friday in the town of Lent.
The bus was carrying 43 passengers, including 15 children, the Bourg-en-Bresse prosecutor's office said.

articles.title_original: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
articles.title_zh: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
facts_zh:
Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
- Published
A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.
Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".
Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity.

all_titles.en: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people

articles.title_zh: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
facts_zh:
Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
- Published
The "Male State", an extremist misogynistic group named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, has denied any link to the false warnings causing flight disruption across Europe.

The comments to the BBC came as reports of more bomb scares to airlines began appearing, including on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon and a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome which was diverted to Venice.

Bomb threats were also reported to a number of high-profile Irish media organisations on Friday, prompting evacuations and a statement from the Irish government suggesting a "co-ordinated campaign of disruption".

all_titles.en: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats

articles.title_original: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
articles.title_zh: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
facts_zh: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.
Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994.
High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party .

all_titles.en: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted

articles.title_original: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
articles.title_zh: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
facts_zh:
Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
- Published
Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a political crisis and a standoff between the presidency and judiciary.
Thursday's ruling came a day after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed - a move which the court said the president lacked the authority to take.
The court also ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, potentially disrupting government plans for nationwide polls next year.

all_titles.en: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis

articles.title_zh: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
facts_zh:
Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
- Published
Iran appears to be undertaking significant new construction near at least two of its major missile sites and repairing bases damaged by months of US and Israeli air strikes, analysis of satellite images suggests.

Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November at the Garmdareh military base in Karaj near the capital Tehran and the Shahroud base in the north, analysts at British intelligence company MAIAR, who reviewed the photos, told BBC Verify.
At least 12 other military sites, including missile complexes and air bases, appear to show signs of repairs.
